steps.title: Prepare growth medium
steps.instruction: Mix 450 mL high‑glucose DMEM (Gibco #41965‑039) with 50 mL fetal calf serum (Sigma #F7524) and add penicillin/streptomycin to a final concentration of 100 U mL⁻¹ penicillin and 100 µg mL⁻¹ streptomycin (use 1× P/S from a 100× stock of 10 000 U mL⁻¹ penicillin and 10 mg mL⁻¹ streptomycin, Gibco #15140122).

steps.title: Passage HEK spCas9+ cells
steps.instruction: When cultures reach 80–90 % confluency, wash the monolayer with 1× PBS (Gibco DPBS, no Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺, #14190‑094), detach cells using 1× Trypsin‑EDTA (Sigma #59418C) diluted in 1× PBS, resuspend in fresh supplemented DMEM and reseed at a 1:10 ratio every third day, incubating at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until confluency is reached again.

steps.title: Prepare starvation and stimulation media
steps.instruction: Dissolve amino‑acid‑free RPMI 1640 powder (USB #R8999‑04A) and leucine‑free RPMI 1640 powder (USB #R8999‑03) in DNase/RNase‑free distilled water according to the manufacturers’ instructions. Supplement each with 2 g L⁻¹ sodium bicarbonate (Sigma #S5761) and 1× penicillin/streptomycin. Add 800 mg L⁻¹ sodium phosphate (Sigma #S5136) to the amino‑acid‑free medium and 2 mM glutamine (Sigma #G7513) to the leucine‑free medium. Use 1 % (v/v) dialyzed FCS (Gibco #26400) and adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 M NaOH (AppliChem #1432). For stimulation, use standard RPMI 1640 (Gibco #21875034) with 1 % dFCS and 1× P/S; for leucine stimulation add leucine (Sigma #L8912) dissolved in 1 M HCl to 380 mM (1000× stock) to achieve the desired final concentration. Perform starvation and stimulation at the times indicated in the results, using cells at 70–80 % confluency.

steps.title: Co‑transfect donor and sgRNA plasmids
steps.instruction: Co‑transfect HEK spCas9+ cells with the nLAP donor plasmid (containing the NGFRETD‑P2A‑nLAP cassette flanked by tia1l sites) and a plasmid expressing the target‑locus‑specific sgRNA (e.g., pLentiCRISPRv2ΔspCas9_BFP). Use a standard transfection reagent and protocol appropriate for Lenti‑X 293T cells.

steps.title: Stain cells with anti‑NGFR‑APC antibody
steps.instruction: Prepare a sterile staining buffer consisting of 1× PBS (pH 7.2) with 0.5 % BSA and 2 mM EDTA (pH 8.0). Four to five days after transfection, remove medium from ~100 % confluent cultures, wash once with 1× PBS, discard PBS and add 3 mL staining buffer for ~1.5 × 10⁷ cells (do not use trypsin). Rock gently until cells detach, transfer the suspension to a sterile tube, and rinse the plate with additional staining buffer if needed. Add 10 µL anti‑human NGFR antibody (APC‑conjugated, Miltenyi #130‑116‑497) to the cell suspension, mix well and incubate 30 min in the dark at 4 °C. Wash by adding 3 mL staining buffer, centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in an appropriate volume of staining buffer for sorting. For a control, stain wild‑type cells using 500 000 cells in 100 µL staining buffer with 1 µL anti‑NGFR‑APC antibody.

steps.title: FACS sort NGFR‑positive cells
steps.instruction: Using a flow cytometer, gate on the highest 5 % NGFR‑APC‑positive population, using the stained wild‑type cells as a negative control. Collect the sorted cells and immediately sub‑culture them at an appropriate density in growth medium (DMEM + 10 % FCS + 1× Pen/Strep). Examine the plates daily until individual colonies become visible.

steps.title: Verify tag integration by PCR and sequencing
steps.instruction: Design primers to amplify (a) the 3′ junction of the nLAP tag (PCR A), (b) the 5′ junction between the target 5′‑UTR and the nLAP tag (PCR C), and (c) the wild‑type allele as a control (PCR B). Perform PCR on genomic DNA from each clone, run the products on an agarose gel, and send the amplicons for Sanger sequencing to confirm in‑frame integration and absence of unwanted indels.

steps.title: Confirm protein expression by Western blot
steps.instruction: Lyse PCR‑confirmed clones, separate proteins by SDS‑PAGE, transfer to a membrane and probe with anti‑GFP antibodies and anti‑WDR59 antibodies (loading control: GAPDH).

steps.title: Assess GFP fluorescence by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Analyze the same clones by flow cytometry, measuring GFP fluorescence (excitation 488 nm, emission 530/30 nm). Use FlowJo v7.6.5 for data analysis and compare mean fluorescence intensity to wild‑type HEK spCas9+ cells.

steps.title: Co‑immunoprecipitate GFP‑tagged protein
steps.instruction: Seed 5 × 10⁶ HEK WDR59‑NGFRETD‑nLAP cells in a 10 cm dish with 10 mL growth medium and grow to ~80 % confluency. Wash cells with cold 1× PBS, discard PBS and add 400 µL CoIP buffer (supplemented) per plate. Scrape cells, transfer to centrifuge tubes, incubate on ice 30 min, then centrifuge at 15 000 rpm (≈2 767 × g). Measure protein concentration of the supernatant (Bradford assay). Incubate 1 000–3 000 µg protein with 25 µL GFP‑Trap magnetic agarose beads (ChromoTek) overnight at 4 °C on a rotating wheel; include an equal volume of control magnetic agarose beads. Wash beads five times with CoIP buffer using a magnetic stand. Elute by boiling beads in 10–15 µL 4× SDS loading dye at 95 °C for 5 min, then resolve on SDS‑PAGE and transfer to a blotting membrane for downstream analysis.
